passages.title: Passage: first-order decomposition
passages.body: A substance $\ce{A}$ decomposes by first-order kinetics, $\ce{A -> products}$, with a rate constant $k = 0.0693\ \text{min}^{-1}$ at a fixed temperature. Answer the following questions based on this information. (Take $\ln 2 = 0.693$.)

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: The physical quantity having the same dimensional formula as Planck's constant $h$ is

solutions.body:
From $E = h\nu$,
$$[h] = \frac{[E]}{[\nu]} = \frac{[ML^2T^{-2}]}{[T^{-1}]} = [ML^2T^{-1}]$$
Angular momentum $L = mvr$ has dimensions $[M][LT^{-1}][L] = [ML^2T^{-1}]$, the same as $h$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Taking $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ and neglecting air resistance, the maximum height reached by the ball is

solutions.body:
At the highest point $v = 0$. Using $v^2 = u^2 - 2gh$:
$$h = \frac{u^2}{2g} = \frac{(20)^2}{2 \times 10} = 20\ \text{m}$$

questions.subject: physics
questions.body:
A block of mass $2\ \text{kg}$ is released from rest on a smooth inclined plane making an angle of $30^\circ$ with the horizontal, as shown. Taking $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, the acceleration of the block along the incline is

![Block of mass 2 kg resting on a smooth plane inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal](diagram:incline-30)

solutions.body:
On a smooth incline the only force along the plane is the component of gravity, $mg\sin\theta$. Hence
$$a = g\sin 30^\circ = 10 \times \tfrac{1}{2} = 5\ \text{m s}^{-2}$$
The acceleration is independent of the mass.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body:
In the circuit shown, resistors of $6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ are connected in parallel, and the combination is in series with a $4\ \Omega$ resistor across an ideal $12\ \text{V}$ battery. The current (in ampere) drawn from the battery is ______.

![Circuit diagram: a 12 V battery connected to a parallel pair of 6 ohm and 3 ohm resistors followed by a 4 ohm resistor in series](diagram:circuit-6-3-4)

solutions.body:
Parallel combination: $R_p = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{6 + 3} = 2\ \Omega$.

Total resistance: $R = 2 + 4 = 6\ \Omega$.

Current: $I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{12}{6} = 2\ \text{A}$.

Conductance of the parallel pair is $\tfrac{1}{6} + \tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{1}{2}\ \text{S}$, so $R_p = 2\ \Omega$. With the $4\ \Omega$ resistor in series the circuit is a $1:2$ voltage divider: $4\ \text{V}$ across the pair and $8\ \text{V}$ across $4\ \Omega$, so $I = 8/4 = 2\ \text{A}$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: An object is placed $30\ \text{cm}$ in front of a thin convex lens of focal length $20\ \text{cm}$. The distance (in cm) of the image from the lens is ______.

solutions.body:
Using the lens formula with $u = -30\ \text{cm}$ and $f = +20\ \text{cm}$:
$$\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{30} = \frac{1}{60}$$
So $v = +60\ \text{cm}$ (real image on the other side of the lens).

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: For an ideal monoatomic gas, the ratio of specific heats $\gamma = C_p / C_v$ is

solutions.body: A monoatomic gas has 3 translational degrees of freedom, so $C_v = \tfrac{3}{2}R$ and $C_p = C_v + R = \tfrac{5}{2}R$. Therefore $\gamma = \dfrac{5/2}{3/2} = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The number of moles of carbon dioxide present in $11\ \text{g}$ of $\ce{CO2}$ is ______. (Molar mass of $\ce{CO2}$ = $44\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$)

solutions.body: $n = \dfrac{m}{M} = \dfrac{11}{44} = 0.25\ \text{mol}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The hybridisation of the central sulphur atom in $\ce{SF6}$ is

solutions.body: Sulphur forms six $\sigma$ bonds with fluorine and has no lone pair, giving six electron domains around S. Six domains correspond to $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation and an octahedral geometry.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body:
For the cell reaction
$$\ce{Zn(s) + Cu^2+(aq) -> Zn^2+(aq) + Cu(s)}$$
the standard electrode potentials are $E^\circ_{\ce{Zn^2+/Zn}} = -0.76\ \text{V}$ and $E^\circ_{\ce{Cu^2+/Cu}} = +0.34\ \text{V}$. The standard emf of the cell is

solutions.body:
Zinc is oxidised (anode) and copper ions are reduced (cathode):
$$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10\ \text{V}$$

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: $4\ \text{g}$ of $\ce{NaOH}$ is dissolved in $500\ \text{g}$ of water. The molality of the solution (in $\text{mol kg}^{-1}$) is ______. (Molar mass of $\ce{NaOH}$ = $40\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$)

solutions.body:
Moles of solute $= 4/40 = 0.1\ \text{mol}$; mass of solvent $= 0.5\ \text{kg}$.
$$m = \frac{0.1}{0.5} = 0.2\ \text{mol kg}^{-1}$$

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body:
The major product of the reaction of propene with $\ce{HBr}$ in the absence of peroxide is
$$\ce{CH3-CH=CH2 + HBr -> ?}$$

solutions.body: In the absence of peroxide, addition follows Markovnikov's rule: $\ce{H+}$ adds to the terminal carbon to give the more stable secondary carbocation $\ce{CH3-\overset{+}{C}H-CH3}$, which is captured by $\ce{Br-}$ to give 2-bromopropane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The oxidation state of iron in $\ce{K4[Fe(CN)6]}$ is

solutions.body:
Let the oxidation state of Fe be $x$. Each $\ce{K}$ is $+1$ and each $\ce{CN-}$ is $-1$:
$$4(+1) + x + 6(-1) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; x = +2$$

answer.note: Sample record illustrating correction history: the editorial key was corrected from C to A after review.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$, then $\alpha^2 + \beta^2$ equals

solutions.body:
$\alpha + \beta = 5$ and $\alpha\beta = 6$, so
$$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha+\beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta = 25 - 12 = 13$$

questions.body: The value of $(1 + i)^8$, where $i = \sqrt{-1}$, is

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body:
The value of the determinant
$$\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$$
is ______.

solutions.body: The matrix is upper triangular, so its determinant is the product of the diagonal entries: $1 \times 1 \times 5 = 5$.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: The value of $\displaystyle\int_0^1 \left(3x^2 + 2x\right)\,dx$ is ______.

solutions.body: $\int_0^1 3x^2\,dx = 1$ (area under $3x^2$) and $\int_0^1 2x\,dx = 1$ (a right triangle with base 1 and height 2). The sum is $2$.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: Two fair dice are thrown together. The probability that the sum of the numbers shown is $7$ is

solutions.body: Favourable outcomes: $(1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1)$ — six of the $36$ equally likely outcomes. $P = 6/36 = 1/6$.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: The angle between the vectors $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j}$ is

solutions.body: $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = (1)(2) + (2)(-1) + (2)(0) = 0$. A zero dot product between non-zero vectors means they are perpendicular, so the angle is $90^\circ$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: The moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about an axis tangent to its surface is

solutions.body:
About a diameter $I_{cm} = \tfrac{2}{5}MR^2$. By the parallel-axis theorem with $d = R$:
$$I = \tfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + MR^2 = \tfrac{7}{5}MR^2$$

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: An isolated conducting sphere of radius $R$ carries a charge $Q$. Taking $k = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}$ and the potential at infinity as zero, which of the following statements is/are correct?

solutions.body: Charge resides on the surface of a conductor, so $E = 0$ inside (A correct). Since $E = -dV/dr = 0$, the potential inside equals its surface value $kQ/R$ (B correct; D wrong). Just outside, the sphere acts like a point charge: $E = kQ/R^2$ (C correct).

options.label: A
options.body: The electric field everywhere inside the sphere is zero.

options.label: B
options.body: The potential everywhere inside the sphere is $\dfrac{kQ}{R}$.

options.label: C
options.body: The magnitude of the electric field just outside the surface is $\dfrac{kQ}{R^2}$.

options.label: D
options.body: The potential at the centre of the sphere is zero.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: A block of mass $1\ \text{kg}$ attached to a light spring of force constant $100\ \text{N m}^{-1}$ oscillates on a smooth horizontal surface. The time period of oscillation, in seconds, correct to two decimal places, is ______.

solutions.body:
$$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{1}{100}} = \frac{2\pi}{10} \approx 0.628\ \text{s} \approx 0.63\ \text{s}$$
Answers in the range $0.62$–$0.64$ are accepted to allow for rounding of $\pi$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: Match each physical quantity in List-I with its dimensional formula in List-II and choose the correct option.

solutions.body:
- Force $= ma \Rightarrow [MLT^{-2}]$ (3)
- Pressure $= F/A \Rightarrow [ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$ (1)
- Work $= F\cdot d \Rightarrow [ML^2T^{-2}]$ (4)
- Impulse $= F\,\Delta t \Rightarrow [MLT^{-1}]$ (2)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The half-life of the reaction, in minutes, is ______.

solutions.body: For a first-order reaction $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k} = \dfrac{0.693}{0.0693} = 10\ \text{min}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The time, in minutes, required for $75\%$ of the reactant to be consumed is ______.

solutions.body: $75\%$ completion leaves $25\% = (1/2)^2$ of the reactant, i.e. two half-lives: $2 \times 10 = 20\ \text{min}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The pH of a $1.0 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{M}$ aqueous solution of $\ce{HCl}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ is ______.

solutions.body: $\ce{HCl}$ is a strong acid, so $[\ce{H+}] = 10^{-3}\ \text{M}$ (water's contribution is negligible). $\text{pH} = -\log_{10}(10^{-3}) = 3$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: Which of the following give(s) a positive Tollens' test (silver mirror)?

solutions.body: Aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent, so formaldehyde (A) and acetaldehyde (B) give a silver mirror. Formic acid (D) contains an aldehyde-like $\ce{H-C(=O)-}$ group and is also oxidised. Acetone (C), a ketone, does not respond.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x) = |x|$. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

solutions.body: $\lim_{x\to0}|x| = 0 = f(0)$, so $f$ is continuous at $0$ (A). The left derivative is $-1$ and the right derivative is $+1$, so $f$ is not differentiable at $0$ (B false). $|x| \ge 0 = f(0)$, so the minimum is at $0$ (C). $f(-x) = f(x)$, so $f$ is even, not odd (D false).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: The sum of the first $n$ terms of the arithmetic progression $2, 5, 8, \ldots$ is $155$. The value of $n$ is ______.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: A fair coin is tossed three times. The probability of getting at least one head, correct to two decimal places, is ______.

solutions.body: $P(\text{no head}) = (1/2)^3 = 1/8$, so $P(\text{at least one head}) = 1 - 1/8 = 7/8 = 0.875$. Both $0.87$ and $0.88$ are accepted as two-decimal roundings.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body:
**Assertion (A):** The acceleration due to gravity decreases as we move upward from the surface of the Earth.

**Reason (R):** Outside the Earth, $g = \dfrac{GM}{r^2}$, which decreases as the distance $r$ from the centre increases.

solutions.body: Both statements are true, and the inverse-square dependence of $g$ on $r$ (R) is exactly why $g$ falls with altitude (A). Hence option A.

options.label: A
options.body: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.body: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.body: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.body: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: The energy of a photon of wavelength $620\ \text{nm}$ is approximately (take $hc = 1240\ \text{eV nm}$)

solutions.body: $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \dfrac{1240\ \text{eV nm}}{620\ \text{nm}} = 2\ \text{eV}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The total number of orbitals in the shell with principal quantum number $n = 3$ is

solutions.body: The number of orbitals in a shell is $n^2 = 3^2 = 9$ (one $3s$, three $3p$ and five $3d$).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body:
For the equilibrium
$$\ce{N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g)}$$
$K_p$ and $K_c$ are related by $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$. The value of $\Delta n$ is

solutions.body: $\Delta n = n_{\text{gaseous products}} - n_{\text{gaseous reactants}} = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$.

questions.subject: biology
questions.body: Which cell component is the site of protein synthesis?

solutions.body: Ribosomes translate messenger RNA into polypeptide chains, so they are the site of protein synthesis. Lysosomes digest material, the Golgi apparatus packages proteins, and centrioles organise the spindle.

questions.subject: biology
questions.body:
**Assertion (A):** Mitochondria are called the powerhouses of the cell.

**Reason (R):** Mitochondria contain their own circular DNA.

solutions.body: Both statements are true. Mitochondria are called powerhouses because aerobic respiration in them produces most of the cell's ATP; possessing their own DNA does not explain this role. Hence option B.

options.label: A
options.body: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.body: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.body: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.body: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: biology
questions.body: In a double-stranded DNA molecule, adenine makes up 20% of the bases. The percentage of guanine is

solutions.body: By Chargaff's rule $A = T = 20\%$, so $G + C = 60\%$ and, since $G = C$, $G = 30\%$.

questions.subject: biology
questions.body: The vector that transmits the malarial parasite to humans is

solutions.body: *Plasmodium* is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected female *Anopheles* mosquito.

questions.subject: biology
questions.body: In $\ce{C4}$ plants, the primary acceptor of $\ce{CO2}$ in mesophyll cells is

solutions.body: In the Hatch–Slack pathway, PEP in mesophyll cells fixes $\ce{CO2}$ (via PEP carboxylase) to form the 4-carbon OAA. RuBP is the acceptor in the Calvin cycle, which occurs in bundle-sheath cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.body:
The pyramid of energy below has four trophic levels. If the producers fix $10{,}000\ \text{J}$ and the 10 per cent law applies, the energy available at the fourth trophic level ($T_4$) is

![Pyramid of energy with producers at the base holding 10,000 joules, followed by primary consumers, secondary consumers and a fourth trophic level at the apex](diagram:energy-pyramid)

| Trophic level | Energy |
|---|---|
| $T_1$ (producers) | $10{,}000\ \text{J}$ |
| $T_2$ | ? |
| $T_3$ | ? |
| $T_4$ | ? |

solutions.body: Only about 10% passes to each higher level: $10{,}000 \to 1000 \to 100 \to 10\ \text{J}$ at $T_4$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop of radius $r$ carrying a steady current $I$ is

solutions.body: From the Biot–Savart law, every element of the loop is at distance $r$ and perpendicular to the radius, giving $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r^2}(2\pi r) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r}$.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: The value of $\sin 30^\circ \cos 60^\circ + \cos 30^\circ \sin 60^\circ$ is

solutions.body: This is $\sin(30^\circ + 60^\circ) = \sin 90^\circ = 1$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: The escape speed of a body from the surface of a planet depends on

solutions.body: $v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$ depends on the planet's mass $M$ and radius $R$, not on the body's mass or the direction of projection.

options.label: A
options.body: the mass of the body only

options.label: B
options.body: the mass and radius of the planet

options.label: D
options.body: the mass of the body and the radius of the planet

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: Which element has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?

solutions.body: Fluorine has the highest Pauling electronegativity (about 4.0) because of its small size and high effective nuclear charge.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: The coefficient of $x^2$ in the expansion of $(1 + x)^5$ is

solutions.body: The general term is $\binom{5}{r}x^r$; for $r = 2$, $\binom{5}{2} = 10$.

questions.subject: english-proficiency
questions.body: Choose the word closest in meaning to **ABUNDANT**.

solutions.body: *Abundant* means existing in large quantities — *plentiful*. *Scarce* is its antonym.

questions.subject: logical-reasoning
questions.body: Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?

solutions.body: The terms are $n(n+1)$ for $n = 1, 2, \ldots$: $1\cdot2, 2\cdot3, 3\cdot4, 4\cdot5, 5\cdot6$. The next is $6 \cdot 7 = 42$ (differences $4, 6, 8, 10, 12$).

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: The magnetic flux through a coil decreases uniformly from $0.5\ \text{Wb}$ to $0.1\ \text{Wb}$ in $0.2\ \text{s}$. The magnitude of the induced emf is

solutions.body: $|\varepsilon| = \left|\dfrac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}\right| = \dfrac{0.5 - 0.1}{0.2} = 2\ \text{V}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: A process at constant temperature and pressure is spontaneous when

solutions.body: At constant $T$ and $p$, the criterion for spontaneity is a decrease in Gibbs energy: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin 3x}{x}$ equals

solutions.body: $\dfrac{\sin 3x}{x} = 3\cdot\dfrac{\sin 3x}{3x} \to 3 \cdot 1 = 3$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: In Young's double-slit experiment, the wavelength of light is $600\ \text{nm}$, the slit separation is $1\ \text{mm}$ and the screen is $1\ \text{m}$ away. The fringe width is

solutions.body: $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d} = \dfrac{600\times10^{-9} \times 1}{1\times10^{-3}} = 6\times10^{-4}\ \text{m} = 0.6\ \text{mm}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The number of structural isomers of $\ce{C4H10}$ is

solutions.body: n-Butane and isobutane (2-methylpropane): two structural isomers.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: The peak value of a sinusoidal alternating voltage is $10\sqrt{2}\ \text{V}$. Its rms value is

solutions.body: $V_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\ \text{V}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: Glucose is classified as

solutions.body: Glucose, $\ce{C6H12O6}$, has six carbon atoms and an aldehyde group: an aldohexose. Fructose is a ketohexose.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: When a p-n junction diode is forward biased, the width of its depletion region

solutions.body: Forward bias opposes the built-in potential, pushing majority carriers towards the junction and narrowing the depletion region.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The oxidation state of manganese in $\ce{KMnO4}$ is

solutions.body: $+1 + x + 4(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +7$.

questions.body: Choose the correct word to fill in the blank: "Neither of the two boys ______ present yesterday."

solutions.body: *Neither* is singular and the sentence is in the past tense, so the verb is *was*.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: The oxidation state of chromium in $\ce{K2Cr2O7}$ is

solutions.body: $2(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow 2x = 12 \Rightarrow x = +6$.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.body: The number of distinct arrangements of the letters of the word LEVEL is

solutions.body: LEVEL has 5 letters with L and E each repeated twice: $\dfrac{5!}{2!\,2!} = \dfrac{120}{4} = 30$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: The gauge pressure at a depth of $10\ \text{m}$ in water (density $1000\ \text{kg m}^{-3}$, $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$) is

solutions.body: $p = \rho g h = 1000 \times 10 \times 10 = 10^5\ \text{Pa}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: With the Lucas reagent (anhydrous ZnCl₂ in concentrated HCl), turbidity appears immediately at room temperature for

solutions.body: Tertiary alcohols form stable tertiary carbocations, so the insoluble alkyl chloride separates almost immediately. Secondary alcohols take a few minutes; primary alcohols do not react appreciably at room temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.body: A force of $5\ \text{N}$ acts perpendicular to a spanner at a distance of $2\ \text{m}$ from the axis. The magnitude of the torque is

solutions.body: $\tau = rF\sin 90^\circ = 2 \times 5 = 10\ \text{N m}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.body: An $S_N2$ reaction at a chiral carbon proceeds with

solutions.body: In $S_N2$ the nucleophile attacks from the side opposite the leaving group in a single step, giving Walden inversion of configuration.

options.label: D
